source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recommend switching to another combustible tobacco product, because changing products is an evidence-based substitute for tobacco cessation.","B":"Recommend 1-800-QUIT-NOW, which connects callers to free, confidential quitline counseling and individualized tobacco-cessation support today.","C":"Advise the client to wait until private counseling is affordable, because free telephone-based cessation services are not available nationwide.","D":"Advise attempting cessation without counseling or medication, because professional support does not improve the likelihood of successful quitting."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC identifies 1-800-QUIT-NOW as a nationwide resource that provides free, confidential quitline counseling and cessation support. Option B is correct. Option A substitutes another combustible tobacco product for cessation. Option C incorrectly claims free nationwide telephone cessation services are unavailable. Option D incorrectly states that counseling or medication support does not improve quit success.
source_row.source_detail: CDC — How to Quit Smoking / Quitlines: 1-800-QUIT-NOW connects callers to free, confidential quitline coaching and cessation support; counseling and cessation medications improve quit success. source_row.stem: A client who smokes cigarettes says, “I want to quit but I cannot afford private counseling.” Which evidence-based resource should the nurse recommend?
